A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HISTOGRAPH work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original HISTOGRAPH results for graph classification, node classification and link prediction, together with ablations, embedding diagnostics and training-runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds inference-runtime measurements in Appendix J and Table 18.

M1.justification: Section 3 broadens input handling: v1 assumes equal-width layer activations, whereas v2 introduces per-layer linear projections for unequal-width activations before stacking. The two attention stages, signed normalization and training modes remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish changes to the models used for retained experiments.

E1.justification: The TU and OGB graph datasets, homophilic and heterophilic node datasets, OGBL-COLLAB and synthetic graph examples are retained. New inference timing reuses MOLHIV and TOXCAST. Appendix G's proposed large-graph scaling strategies are future work, not additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding predictive experiments. Table 18 compares inference runtimes against GMT and MeanPool, which already participate in the training-runtime comparison in Figure 4; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix J adds gradient-free inference timing, reported as milliseconds per epoch, for 3- and 32-layer GCNs on MOLHIV and TOXCAST. v1 reports training timing only. This adds an evaluation procedure without reporting revisions to the retained predictive-evaluation settings.

E4.justification: The component ablations, historical-layer and aggregation ablations, depth tests, embedding diagnostics and synthetic examples retain their evidence. Appendices H and I discuss existing figures and ablations. Appendix J adds runtime benchmarking rather than a new ablation, robustness test or diagnostic intervention.

E5.justification: Existing mean-and-standard-deviation reporting is unchanged. v2 adds no seed counts, repeated-run specifications, confidence intervals or significance procedures. The new inference table reports averages without additional uncertainty information.

E6.justification: Existing table values and plotted results are unchanged. Table 18 adds inference measurements: for 32-layer MOLHIV, HISTOGRAPH reports 3.174 ms versus GMT's 15.158 and MeanPool's 2.130; v1 has no corresponding inference results. Appendix H also newly describes embedding differences as growing with depth, although the retained Figure 2 shows a decreasing trend across layer indices.

T1.justification: Section 3 relaxes the equal-dimensionality assumption and defines per-layer projection maps into a common space. Proposition 1, its Appendix E proof and the filtering equations remain unchanged. Expanded discussion of attention and computational complexity does not add a new theoretical guarantee.

C1.justification: The central contribution and performance claims remain intact, but the conclusion now explicitly qualifies the design as best suited to small-to-medium-sized graphs. Its added reference to OGBL-COLLAB restates link-prediction coverage already claimed and demonstrated in v1.

C2.justification: Appendices G–I add explicit scalability boundaries, interpretations of learned attention and a protein-specific multiscale explanation for the PROTEINS gains. Appendix I additionally claims the existing ablations exclude implementation artifacts, without new controls. Section 5.2 and Appendix J introduce interpretations of inference overhead.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a concrete code-repository address in the abstract; v1 only promises repository availability upon acceptance. Section 3 clarifies input dimensions and positional-encoding broadcasting. Hardware and hyperparameter documentation in Appendices B–C is unchanged; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Wang et al. (2024) in the related-work discussion and Zaheer et al. (2020), Big Bird, for prospective sparse attention. Section 4 more explicitly distinguishes HISTOGRAPH's combination of components from generic attention over representation sequences. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 locally revises notation and explanatory passages, adds Appendices G–J and acknowledgements, and updates publication headers. The main section sequence, contribution list and most existing prose are retained; this is an expansion rather than extensive restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 18 and relocates existing displays through reflow, including Figure 3 and Tables 15–17. Conference headers also change the presentation. Existing figures, table structures and captions are otherwise substantially retained.

improvement.justification: The code address, clearer input formulation, explicit scalability limits and inference measurements improve usability and transparency. However, new Appendix H reverses Figure 2's plotted depth trend, Appendix I claims to exclude implementation artifacts without new controls, and Section 5.2 calls inference overhead negligible despite Table 18 showing 49–119% increases over MeanPool. These additions improve documentation while weakening interpretive accuracy, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
